M: M is a single standing edifice. He’s soft in the middle but that matters not. For all intent and purposes, M is a classless leader.
Mac: Mac is bright, easily bored and not easily forgotten. He's not as lethal business owner, however, and this is probably a blessing. The notion of sacking his employees to save a few bucks would never enter his head.
Macallister: Nice guy. Zero common sense. And he's not on his own, is he Norman?
Macca: See Noelene, although Macca is far less intelligent.
Mace: His voice is deeper than Bronwyn’s although she laughs more. Like Caroline, however, Mace never makes the same mistake twice. And yes, Mace is a man.
Macen: No, he's no sculptor, that's for sure. He has a sense of humour tucked beneath his rather aloof exterior but it takes a while for it to come to the surface. Macen is definitely his own man and he can't really be badgered into doing anything he doesn't want to do. Having said that, he'll move with the pack so long as the pack aren't complete idiots and while not really a natural leader, he'll step up when he needs to. If you offend him deeply once, then you won't get the chance to do it again.
Mack: Mack is too industrious and worldly to become an ambulance driver, but many of his friends rib him about such a possibility, such is the general level of empathy he feels towards friends and strangers alike. He doesn't tolerate corruption of any kind and one day he'll sail across the Pacific Ocean in a yacht he built himself. Not bad eh? Hell, he might even raise his family in such a place.
Mackie: Sure, he might be a fish scientist but that’s just one part of it. Mackie is full of empathy and love and good humour, just don’t let him smoke the evil weed or drink too much coz’ then he’ll start talking and when his blood is running hot he may not stop the sun is up the following morning. On top of that, he is intensely loyal, he prefers old cars to new and he is often quite secretive about his creative pursuits.
Maclayne: Maclayne is the kind of man who will buy a car from the car lot based purely on how shiny it is. He won't even try turning the thing on. We've no idea how he gets on in the world romantically. We suspect it'd be lot's of fun and bubbles in the first two weeks, followed by torment, screaming and ultimate tragedy during the ensuing three.
Macson: Guarded he might be, just a little bit, but it’s a wild ride to get to adulthood. He’s healthy now and looking great - fit and strong too - but actions have reactions and he understands his surrounds faster now than ever before. Once he trusts you you're in. And he's a good friend to have.
Madava: Yep, he's a man, a caring an interesting man, and his name is Madava. His name is slow and loping, which is how he walks, and he thinks deeply, ruminating for a long time before he speaks. Rest assured, Madava will never sit in an office working for 'the man'. No sir. Hopefully he ran off with the circus, or with whichever metaphorical artistic  group arrived first. Amen.
Maddaggain: Maddaggain, is that a watch on your wrist or a miniature fucking circus. Seriously man, we can see that thing from space. Do you really think it's going to get you laid?
Maddex: Far from being just ornamental, Maddex is a constantly-moving shit-stirrer who never dies wondering what might have been. So, he’s here, he’s there, and his enthusiasm for life means he’s always welcomed, no matter how brief his stays are.
Maddox: Maddox is a smart alex, I mean, a smart alec. As a low-level hustler and swindler, he knows all the dodgy blokes down at the smokey end of the bar and he agrees to nothing without settling on a price first. If armageddon happens and humans are reduced to a scrapping, fight-to-the-end state of living, then Maddox will do just fine.
Madisch: Madisch abhors morose or overtly shy people. If a  situation isn’t to your liking, either fix it or shut up: this is his motto, and rightly so. His life is usually a cavalcade of busyness and laughter, and invigorating ideas. If you have some ongoing issue I’m not sure I’d go to Madisch for a shoulder to cry on, well, unless you’re a pretty girl, but if you’ve a great idea about some new genius start-up company, get him on board for sure. He parties long and hard, and he seems to cope with the hangovers better than most.
Madison: You must be happy they didn't call you Angela, eh? As a fellow with a very feminine name, Madison has evolved into quite a forgiving and caring individual. God knows we need more of them. He’ll certainly never be the over-seer of any kind of Eastern European slavery racket, thankfully.
Magnus: The name of large, flawless diamond sitting patiently and quietly upon a blue velvet pillow.
Maine: Why is everyone calling their children the names of American states? Maine, did your mum love Stephen King? Is that it? Anyway, it's made you an occasionally intolerant and bored-looking fellow who doesn't smile enough. Then again, perhaps it's a result of you wishing your parents lived in another country? I'm not sure.
Malachi: (Pron. Malakai) Ah, if only his name was spelt like that. If Malachi had his shit together then he’d be amazing – perhaps he is not meant to – but like one or two other prodigal sons within the realm, Malachi is wasteful and he lacks foresight.
Malcolm: A chunk of wood about six feet long that’s lying on the floor. He’s rich in colour, heavy in weight and, how are you Malcolm?
Mali:
Now Mali, life can be easy and super cruisy, as you know, but the real fun and the great moments of self-discovery occur when you confront those things that scare you. Your task then, young man, is go forth into the world, with or without your large group of friends - preferably without, because some of them are pretty lazy too - find out what those things are and then charge them head on.

(Note: Please retain some common sense in these said adventures and we'll talk about assisting those in need a little bit more, a bit later on.)
Mance: Is Mance breezy? Is Mance carefree? These are questions those who have just met him will ask his closer friends and they will answer that, on the surface, yes he is. Like a well-designed shop front, Mance provides the facade to the world which does the job, but there are fingers in pies and schemes afoot in the back rooms, make no mistake. (Not illegal or dangerous schemes by the way. Just smart, speculative ones.)
Manfred:
Manfred wears Ralph Lauren polo shirts with the collar up and a big chunky, silver watch. Does he possess a small, expensive car collection? Perhaps. 
He’s rarely short, he thinks all women always love him and his kids attend a very expensive private schools.
Mani: Owns greyhounds. Races them too, and only rarely does he give them a bit of special 'racing juice' on the morning of the meet.
Manju: Manju has tattoos - who doesn't these days? - and he's into his music big-time. Does he make money out of it? Not quite but he'll get there. He has a large cheesy grin and when he hears a funky beat his head starts moving as separate from his body like a chicken looking for feed.
Manning:
Manning is only one or two disasters from being wind-swept and weather beaten. What the hell are you talking about, you ask? Well, Manning is a formal man, and formalities by definition, at some point, invite a person to act in a way that isn’t truly natural. I mean, who cares if your dinner partner licks their plate? Who cares what brand shirt your wearing? All this inane concern about nothing takes a toll after a while. It’s just not real, Manning. You want our advice? Throw out all your suits immediately and go visit a nudist camp for a week. You might come back a different, and are more relaxed and splendid individual. 
Amen.
Mannix: “Don’t tell ‘em I was here and if they ask where you got them, just say Tony found them.”…..Mannix is involved in these kinds of conversations often.
Manny: Manny rarely travels 2nd class, and this despite the bad language and the lewd gestures.
Manta: Like his namesake beneath the waves Manta moves without seemingly doing anything. He switches jobs and girlfriends without a whisper and always seems to be smiling. Maybe he smokes a lot of pot, we’re not sure, but he doesn't have a career as such, we can tell you that.
Manu:
"Me Manu, you Jane. You come with me. You come to jungle, now.”
(Jane, et al not happy.)
Marc: The Principal Artist with the Melbourne/Chicago/Geneva Ballet Company.
Marcel: ‘Marcel’ is what happens to a person when they come back from the optometrist with their first pair of new spectacles. Suddenly, you have clarity, you sense things you never sensed before and, most important, you have time. (In person, Marcel therefore never rushes, his deepest thoughts are kept to himself and the most outlandish thing you might see him do is straddle his deep-black 1200cc motorbike and disappear into the night at a staggering speed.)
Marcellinus: Message from Management: Marcellinus, you’ve spent too much money on pointless material crap. Do you think you’ll worry about any of it on your death bed? It’s time to do some good…
Marcello: Marcello has read too many gangster books. He's not a violent man, per se, but he does love the idea of going to a fine dining restaurant with a gun stuffed down the back of his trousers. Question: Marcello, are you okay?
Marcelo: Marcelo annoints his cock with only the finest oils.
Marco: Marco lost his virginity when he was 11 and having had that much fun as a youngster he therefore refuses to grow up. Can you blame him? These days he wears tight Speedos and waxes his chest, back, buttocks and testicles.
Marcus: Marcus is single-minded and cool in a crisis. ‘Who is Marcus?’ many people ask, and there is a simple answer: Marcus is Marcus. (In a past life he was a gay New Yorker and his full name was Marcus Maximus.)
Marek: Marek has an innocent grin but forget the facade for he’s nearly always near the middle of whatever shit-storm is going down. He just likes to see what will happen, that’s all.
Mariano:
No, he's not a breed of sheep, he's a bouncing pony with a diamond-encrusted bridle who knows full well that this part of the circus performance is screwed without him. 

Just have a look at that strut!...
Mario: Mario is a hyena that lives a pack existence. Regardless that he might be covered in the blood of a recent kill, he’s as funny as hell on a good day and petulant and short tempered on a bad one. This is the life and this is Mario's niche.
Marius:
Option A:  As a distant relative of the Roman Emperor, Nero, Marius is a predestined leader of men who is skilled at making decisions devoid of emotional involvement. Boring, he may be, but he will tell you that some mild human death and suffering (not to mention plenty of environmental degradation) is a necessary bi-product of any great commercial success.
 
Option B:  Wears hemp clothing. Owns a bead shop.
Mark:
Option A:  Mark is an organised, modern man. Generally he is well-groomed, has friends and is no dummy, and he has a dedicated need to achieve something. As such he is best suited to a life in which there is some high level of diligence and training. He makes a good cop, when there is such a thing, and a capable commercial pilot. He operates quite well under pressure.

Option B:  Hangs out with Greg.
Markham: His folks are academics and Markham was told-off plenty as a little boy. He wrestled with that as he wrestles with all problems and eventually he found his solution: To be happier and more forgiving than they were.
Marko: Eh? Marko? Launch himself out the front of a landing craft and charge up the beach with a bayonet fixed to the front of this rifle? Are you out of your bloody mind? The only time you'll see Marko run at anything is if the horse he backed has won and he wants to beat the rush to collect from the bookmaker. Either that or some parent has surprised he and his lover in the lounge room and he's making a nude dash for the back door.
Markus: Successful in a capitalistic sense, does Markus need a sense of humour more than he currently possesses? Perhaps, or maybe it’s just a bi-product of not feeling the need to associate with people or situations he is remotely bothered by. He’s certainly ambitious, so in that regard it makes sense. Markus is highly intelligent, he dresses very well and as a stylish city bound man he could pass as being gay, straight or indifferent to the whole shebang.
Marky: Marky is a nice bi guy. Clearly, his sexuality is irrelevant but it does highlight the fact that he is true to his heart and true to his friends. He is also smarter and funnier than a very smart, funny person. Marky.
Marlen: Marlen is an interesting bloke who lives the quiet artists’ life. His girlfriends tend to be much younger than him – not to mention physically beautiful – and if he ever gets dumped he knows that all he has to do is relax and get on with life because he always seems to win them back.
Marley: Yep, you guessed it, Marley is Clio's brother and what a wonderful creature he is!
Marli: Oh my god, man. Come on, we're going to climb that mountain there. It's all about getting some fresh air into those lungs and to get those muscles of yours moving. Any longer in front of that bloody device and you're entire body will atrophy so there's nothing left of you but a blob in a jar.
Marlo:
No, he’s not Marlon Brando and he’s not a marlin fish. He’s Marlo. His parents conceived him in the ocean one drunken night and here we are….maybe he does have vestigial fins in his DNA somewhere? Anyway, Marlo isn’t usually comfortable in a crowd. He doesn’t ever count the money in his wallet - indeed, does he even possess one? - and he is amazed (and disappointed) at how nearly everyone in his midst is attempting desperately to accrue some kind of wealth. 

He’d make a good shaman.
Marshall: Organised. Upper-middle class. Thinks he’s a bit special.
Marshy: Marshy lives for the above average heat of some semi-desert. Don't give him snow. Don't give him big brown bears that might eat him. He doesn’t mind hard work, he loves a beer and he has more friends than he knows what to do with, but don't talk shit. You can give him machinery to tinker with if you like, that's fine, but just give him big skies and clean air to breath, okay? Marshy.
Mart: Young at heart and agile, Mart gets just as excited as his kids at the prospect of a trip to anywhere new.
Marthyn: Yep, he gets called Martha all the time and why not - it's a funny, quirky name for someone who needed one. Indeed, Marthyn, forget Marthyn. We like Martha. You cant wipe the smile from his face, no matter how or why it was put there, and overall we want him around.
Martin: Good friends with Simon, Patrick, Chris and Greg. Jonathon, too.
Marto: Marto is an active man. His girlfriends, wives and others, however, while generally adoring Marto’s sense of adventure, his cheeky grin and his loveable nature, know that he possesses the attention span of a fucking goldfish. Yes, he can strategically nod and appear to be listening, but he isn’t. It’s all an act. So, if you’ve got something you need to get off your chest with someone who will listen, I’d head next door.
Marty: The University Prankster who is often short in stature.
Martyn: The name of the special wheelie chalk machine that is used at Wimbledon to mark the white lines on centre court.
Marvin: Is it magic or he a magician? No one is certain, but there aren't nearly enough of them. (And no, sorry, we can't explain him properly either. Management.)
Masie: Just before he has his photo taken, Masie sucks in a big gulp of air and puffs himself up in the same way a clumsy male pigeon fluffs-up his feathers while in pursuit of another bored female.
Mason: Mason is a bit stiff and not from the waist, down. It's the capacity to think laterally in a fluid and relaxed fashion that is at question here. But, he seems to do quite well and he's rarely broke, for some reason….And don’t worry, we don’t get it either.
Mat: Mat the doormat. (Come on dude, time for two Ts.)
Mateo: Boy, is he a thinker. There's a reason for that because there's a reason for everything, right? Mateo probably needs to smile more than he does but no one is perfect. He could certainly do with a couple of meditation techniques to use when his brain starts to overheat.
Mathew: Mathew is the name of a great mountain ravine up in the Himalayas way above the tree line. Hard to get to, it’s an intricately complex place whose difficulty in reaching is matched only by the view that you get once you arrive. Only a select few will ever get to appreciate Mathew’s beauty but it’s an unforgiving environment. If you get injured while you’re up there and the weather closes in, then forget it. You’re doomed. (Note: the number of 't's' is irrelevant, with this boy.)
Matio:
A rather neat individual, this is what Matio isn't: biker, plasterer, rabbit skinner, raw pig eater and sewer worker.

And this is what he could be: designer, architect, engineer, mathematician, psychopath, IT guru.
Matisse: Matisse slides through life with the luck of someone unusually blessed. But it hasn't made him lazy - far from it. Matisse wears his heart on his sleeve and he rarely dies wondering. Yes, he'll wail with a broken heart, but as he'll tell you, stress, pain and anger are much better vented than secretly retained. Lots of friends. Gives good advice.
Matt: Matt observes the world go by with a natural ease. He is sufficiently outgoing and usually highly intelligent, and he never has too many troubles finding romance, but I’ll let you in on a little secret – Matt maybe so competitive that he borders on being occasionally violent!
Mattae: Gallery artist. Street artist. His enthusiasm for everything and everyone means he will stay young for a very long time, probably forever. He attracts women like nobody’s business and no one would be surprised if, via one of the usual random flukes he seems to generate, he inherited about $9 million from some lost uncle or somewhere. Last I heard he was embarking on a job of tattooing his own entire body. Mattae.
Matthew: Listen, fret not. Two Ts = One T, Matthew, so please head on up to your funk soul brother. Management.
Matthias: Yes, he is a polite and sometimes secretive man, but Matthias grunts so loudly when he's making love that he can be heard two floors above and below him. There's an unconfirmed rumour that his lovers learn to wear ear plugs. (We all have a niche to fill, remember.)
Matty: His name falls out of your mouth and zips around the corner to see what he’s missed out on, and what’s about to happen next. Rarely morose and glum for very long, Matty is young at heart but not so immature that he loses sight of those events which are meaningful, despite his occasional spats. As a burgeoning adult he’s doing very well, and certainly his rather massive circle of friends points to this fact.
Maurice:
An indigenous elder who sees ghosts and laughter everywhere. When or if he becomes a ghost himself he will continue to laugh constantly and he will always adore beautiful women. Where are you Maur'? 

(Note: If Maurice is a white man he will clean his car spotlessly every Sunday and for reasons no one has any idea about, he will glean an immense amount of pride from presenting his clean mechanical travel tool to the street. Very odd.)
Maurizio: Scammer. Sure, he's got the smile and the moves and he's a charmer alright. But, yeah, he's a scammer.
Mauro: Mauro sits so still that people have mistaken him for being dead. He can out-stare the best of them.
Maverick: What? Maverick has no blemishes on his record? Who told you that load of nonsense? No, in many ways we're quite proud of Maverick, and how he's managed to stay out of jail for as long as he has. He's not a nasty person though, please don't get that impression. Indeed, we love the way Mav' rushes into things without thinking....then again, he might just grow out of that because that's what we're used to. We'll keep you posted....
Max: This boy is blessed with the letter x in his name that fits in with those around it in an incredibly powerful way. As a result, Max is a wonderfully unusual human being: He is charismatic, sexy and determined, and things just seem to happen when he’s around.
Maxfield: A Cavoodle dog (a King Charles Cavalier crossed with a poodle) that is covered in a mop of silky white hair. If he hears a noise outside he’ll start barking like crazy before bolting out of the kitchen, whereupon he’ll often crash, head first, into the glass sliding doors that he omitted to check were open or not. But the impact never shuts him up for long. The human version is basically identical.
Maxim: Clinical and therefore just a little dull, Maxim is bright enough but what about a smile once in a while brother? I suppose his analytical mind hasn't really stopped since he arrived here on Earth and so perhaps we can’t blame him for looking preoccupied? He’d make a good organic chemist, physicist or mathematician. He possesses a twisted sense of humour.
Maximilian: Is he German? Does he at least possess northern European parents? Anyway, whatever, Maximilian is more sensitive than his name would have you believe. Staunchly loyal, he will never be found begging for money in a Mumbai alley way…well….unless he decides to start smoking opium on his travels, but that’s not really his caper. You see, Maximilian is a clean-living fellow most of the time and his pursuits are usually healthy and profitable.
Maximillian: This fellow is basically identical to his twin brother (Maximilian) so go look him up, except Maximillian has an ever-so-slightly greater chance of being fraudulent, and of being kicked out of any house he is living in, even though this is an unlikely event at the best of times. For what it’s worth, both of them are almost certainly university educated.
Maximus: Once upon a time Maximus owned a  Used Car Dealership. He did quite well, especially given that Nick (said he) did his tax for him. Anyway, that was a long time ago and Maximus has forsaken his tendencies to steal from the mechanically uneducated to stealing from the fiscally irresponsible. Financial management: this is where he resides these days and why oh why Maximus did you forsake your artistic bent?
Maxwell: Maxwell has two pieces of toast with vegemite and a big mug of tea every single morning. Loves crosswords.
Maxy: Maxy is thinking all the time, he is discouraged by useless people and dull deeds, and if the world were to be taken out by that giant meteor that Bryce might rattle on about, Maxy wouldn’t mind so much, so long as he was standing at the spot where it hit the earth so he could watch.
Mazza: Mazza has a giant grin and we don’t think he’d mind us telling you that he is one kinky fucker. Indeed, he’d probably be stoked about it because it might increase his chances of getting lucky with that special lady who can handle that kind of thing. Disregarding his sexual exploits, Mazza actually works pretty hard, unless he detested his boss, in which case he wouldn't mind being fired either. Mazza.
McGregor: Is he a clan leader? Well, no, but he does imagine himself thus, which is why he has something of a presence. He’s not a twat, usually, although he does covet the usual set of material goods that have brainwashed a large chunk of society in general. You can’t blame him for that I guess. McGregor is human like the rest of us. He’s also a funny guy and worth his due.
McKella: McKella has long arms like Roger, although he isn't as furry. A slightly more savvy version of Ronnie, McKella flirts with the white collar end of the law and he's never lifted a brick in his life.
Melvin: Melvin is a party, and how many names are a party?
Memphis: Christ, did your parents duck into a litte alcove on a tour of Elvis's mansion and have it off? Anyway, Memphis is an okay fellow, but he doesn't chew his food enough and rarely is his mouth closed.
Merrick: Merrick rhymes with either Smart Alec or Smart At It. No one is really sure....perhaps it’s a bit of both? In the real world he operates like a big, dumb chocolate lab' whose job is to never ever grow up, to slobber over everything and eat holes in the sides of all the couches. A nightmare to own but bloody fun to visit.
Merv: Merv is a good guy who is there when you need him. If Merv goes to the pub for a friend’s birthday, for example, no matter how many times he himself throws up and no matter how often he gets rejected from entering the disco, afterwards, he’ll stick around outside until he knows that the birthday boy has had a good night.
Mervin: What is reality? – This is Mervin’s personal ethos. Metaphorically or otherwise, Mervin speaks Italian, French, Spanish, German, Swedish and English, he is skilled at metallurgy and wine making and, if attending a large and formal dinner party, he is just as likely to be secretly undoing the $700 bra strap of the Duchess with one hand, while at the same time leading the rest of the table in a resounding rendition from Bizet’s Carmen, with the other.
Micah: Micah dresses neatly, is never seen unshaven in public, he speaks very well and while at university he is the president of a politial club. Very clean hands.
Micha: The debonair mystery man. If you can track down Kenny and ask him how his brain works as it pertains to work and women, and we only suggest him because there are way more Kennys in the wild, then you will go some way as to understanding Micha. Good luck.
Michael:
Catholic school boy. Political advisor/fundraiser. Head engineer. Chief Justice. Airline pilot.....he’s in there somewhere*. 

*(ie- he’s organised, he’s smart and he’s reasonably conservative.)
Micheal:
Successful business deals, political leverage, societial status: these things are important to Micheal and hence form a large portion of his thought processes. That tiny slick of impatience that was provided to him by everyone continually mis-spelling his name as a young man has squeezed out a hard and uncompromising business head in adulthood. Is he tolerant? Sometimes. Does he give to charities very often?
.....Are you serious?
Michelle: French? Dutch? Maybe. Where ever he is from, Michelle is direct, ambitious and knowledgeable. Is he arrogant? Sometimes. A pain in the arse? Occasionally. Funny? Usually. It depends if he thinks you are a twit or not.
Mick: An Australian icon. He’s no rocket scientist – indeed, only physical things that he can touch make sense to him – but his symbol, the fist with the raised thumb, belongs on a flag, somewhere. (Note: He detests being called Mike.)
Mickey: As an amateur boxer, Mickey has tattoos on his back and shoulders, wears a white singlet, sweats a lot and sports a nose that has been broken at least three times.
Micro: If Micro is a big guy he is rather dim, and he almost certainly possesses one special skill involving either brute strength or some gut-churning party trick, like eating a spider before every third tequila shot, for example. If Micro is small, then he is only small in stature. He’s highly intelligent, he’s a gifted strategist and he is constantly thinking about what will happen next. You’ll hear big-Micro walking down the street  from 25 metres away, but little-Micro moves too fast to pin down although I can tell you for a fact he’s doing well, having laid an excellent foundation.
Midge: Midge is less sure of himself than he looks, which is a shame. But he’s an optimistic, compassionate man who rarely gets stuck, be it in a bad relationship, a dodgy part of town or at the back of the queue.
Miguel: Where is he from, this man of dark hair and black, black eye brows? Is he a drifter or does he live here? Anyway, Miguel is a rogue at the bar and, gentlemen, if you're concerened about how you and your girlfriend are going it might pay to keep an eye on him. Ladies, Miguel will love you, even if it's only for one glorious night!
Mika: Mika works for a tech company in robotic research. What he says that they can do already is staggering and it's not all good news for us humans, for the future. But that isn't Mika's business. He's here to do his job, make his robots as well as he can and, hopefully, make as much cash as possible.
Mike: Mike would make an excellent dentist. He is a calming soul who gets on well with people of all ages and who understands the consequences of his actions. He feels slightly uncomfortable when people call him Mick.
Mikey: Perpetually young at heart, Mikey is usually a big, cuddly, friendly guy with no apparent responsibilities whatsoever. If he's thin of stature, however, then he's a lot more competitive and capable than he lets on. And probably not as outgoing.
Mikle: Mikle is similar to his more affluent cousin (Michael) except that he's never been schooled in any form of theology, his ego isn't anything like the same size and he's probably visited more budget gentlemens' clubs.
Milan: Milan has a deep voice and he likes to give the impression that he works too hard
Mile: Pronounced Miele, like the vacuum cleaner, here we have a fellow who is gentle but not feeble. Miele is comfortable and content and despite a rather superior intellect, he is always subtle. Never dates uneducated women.
Miles: Nothing like Myles, Miles is an American ditz.
Milla: A lone, very smart stray cat who saunters into your house like he owns the joint, and who expects cat food, milk, and certainly a bowl of water. No way will he allow you to put a collar and a bell on him but, give him his due, he loves affection and kind words like most of us. Heed this though, if things aren't to his liking for more than 36 hours then you won't see him again. His name is Milla and he's a long way from figuring out what he's doing here. You'll need to be very patient.
Millar: Millar isn't comfortable in a bathroom if the towels aren't draped over the towel rack in a neat and square fashion, and if there are more than one they need to be symmetrical in presentation. At someone’ else’s house he even has to re-align them if they’re not, then he can relax. (If you're talking to him at a party, for instance, and he looks a litte serious or distracted don't take it personally. He's probably just wondering what the towel set-up is like.)
Miller: On the surface everything is shipshape, but this cat can hold a secret, as well as a secret get away plan. Is he a criminal? No, but he’d probably do alright if he became one. The cops and the ladies can never pin him down, which explains why he’s perpetually single, which in turn can be explained by his propensity to never stay in one place for too long.
Milny: See Greig, except there’s nothing aloof about Milny at all.
Milo: Milo works with Dion. He ain’t no builder.
Milton: Have you ever been so hungry when you ate a sandwich that you bit your fingers by mistake? It’s called The Milton Bite and it hurts like shit but, Christ, it’s funny.
Mini: Mini doesn’t squander much, but he’s not anal either. Far from it. For whatever reason, Mini’s name compels  the world to assume that he is never going to be the loudest and most obnoxious person in the room. Which means, therefore, he’s usually the most demure as well as being one of the most pleasant and delightful individuals you will ever meet. Yes, he has an ego but you’d never know, only because even he doesn’t. Mini thinks deeply, rarely acts impulsively and always considers others before he acts. Not bad for a man with a ‘little’ name, eh?
Mirek: The splendid Joker in any deck of cards. His specialty is lewd European trash jokes.
Misel: As a father he's a little over-bearing. Sure, we all expect our kids to be great and to turn out well, but they have to be free to make their own mistakes in their own time. I suppose it makes sense Misel is a bit harsh in this life, sometimes, because he spent several past lives in villages across Europe, several hundred years ago, living in very tough conditions and being regularly raided by bands of brigands. He has a sense of humour, you just have to dig a bit to find it, that's all.
Misko: The loud, humorous and wholly inappropriate restaurant owner who ensures most of his takings don’t go through the till.
Mitch: Mitch is a gregarious and energetic man. He surfs, he does maths and he has a well- rounded grasp of both the world and his place in it. Like his more unforgiving brother, below, he also knows how to get what he wants although he won’t go as far as killing anyone in order to get it.
Mitt: Mitt is the name of that donkey that you're about to ride out into the desert, en route to a drug deal with a Mexican cartel that'd soon as shoot you rather than look at you. There's going to be ten of them and only one of you, no one's around, and I'm SURE they'll give you all those drugs after taking all your money. They're fine upstanding men, aren't they? They wouldn't go back on their word, would they? I mean, they're business men, right?.... (Moral to the story? Mitt, think.)
MJ: Like a slippery eel that knows where it's going, M.J can bend and slide and allow the energies around him to work for him, not against him. He struggles on land, though. (That is, in any kind of organised, repetitive situation, like a 9 to 5 job, for instance.)
Moeseno: The undercover master who is peculiar, honest to the tune of 81% and exact. A little narrow-minded at times.
Moffat: A betting man who loves the company of betting men.
Molly: This boy is soft at his core but he is idealistic and reckless on the surface. Gently, gently Molly....
Monte:
Built for the big occasion, Monte is the kind of fellow who will walk into a S&M club for the first time shitting himself and swearing black and blue that there’s no way he’s getting his kit off for anyone, and not 30 minutes later he’s being gloriously whipped by a startling Amazonian-looking woman while at the time being anally probed by a different lady and her special hand-held device. 

Make no mistake, Monte is destined to live a fulfilled and interesting life, none of which is boring or forgetful, and many could take a leaf out of his book.
Monty: You guessed it; Monty has a giant silver ring pierced through his knob. It's why he speaks so well and so extravagantly - he's constantly feeling it as he talks. Weird, huh?
Moot: Moot left a town of about 4 people leaving 3, somewhere out in the middle of nowhere, and soon found himself cleaning the bottom of ferries next to a jetty while wearing SCUBA gear. Being from frontier country, he used a frontier-style method to perve on women. As the customers boarded the ferry, he would position himself under the jetty and perve upwards with the reg’ in his mouth, and every time he spied a girl in a short skirt or a dress, he’d yell out ‘Moot!!’ at the top of his voice. It’s a miracle he wasn’t arrested.
Mop: Mop is a simple fellow but don’t be fooled for he is a switched-on operator who has secret plans no one knows about.
Morani: Some advice if you’re about to give Morani the sack: Try not to criticise anything about him, and not even to his friends if you happen to see them later. That’s all I’m saying. It’s his Maori blood that makes him that way……we think. Good luck!
Morgan: Morgan carries an attitude that stems from old family money and, fortunately or unfortunately, plenty is expected of him.
Morris: Conservative and stern, Morris has strict moral values. He could probably recite most of the decent psalms from the bible.
Morten: Morten is a calm, quirky and funny individual. As such he is likely to be an investigator of the universe within one of the fields of oceanography, meteorology or biology.
Moscow: There’s nothing Russian about him – apart from his love of Vodka – and while he is definitely not normal he looks to get on with life and have as much filthy fun as possible. The last time anyone saw him alive he was being dragged alone into a tent by three gorgeous young nubiles.
Mossy:
Mossy isn’t from the city, and he'd prefer a beer to any other kind of drink, and he'd rather sleep in than get up and deal with life sometimes, but when he did he'd put in a good effort, grumbling only rarely, and he has a better than vague idea about cars and how they work (not these new ones though). Perhaps best of all he has an easy smile and people like him. As do his kids, even though they give him shit about him never growing up.

Such is life. Such is Mossy.
Muchy: The wonderful ancient God of mirth, music and profitable betting who can’t sit in the same spot for more than about 11 minutes. He’s also known as the Host with the Most and arguably the best tour manager to have ever lived.
Munro: Astute and more delicate than you imagine, in a past life Munro was a splendid alpaca. He looks out for his team, he confronts problems head on and he retains a sense of humour in all but the most dire of predicaments.
Muppet: The name given to any man by a woman with a sense of humour and who loves him deeply, and who expects him to mow the lawn and mend things around the house. And, of course, to be playful when it counts. :)
Murdoch: Murdoch doesn't just like to win, he likes to pulverise the opposition. If he's a short man then he suffers from the syndrome terribly. Usually, however, he wears a suit and tie and he does nothing for free.
Murphy: Loves a decent wine bar on Friday night. The clubs are too loud for him.
Murray: The Murray is the phenomenon of dropping a bucket that is half filled with mud. After it hits the ground most of it slops straight up and hits you in the face as you stand there. “Oh, Murray!” you cry. He’s tolerated in the country, indeed he’s very funny, but city folk just don’t understand him.
Mustufah: By definition, Mustufah is hard-working and conscientious. He might even be a little too forgiving occasionally, but the traditions around his family are very important and take precedence over the rest of his life.
Muzz: Kinky and thoughtful, Muzz is one of the boys but he’s not an idiot, and he’s definitely not lacking in available love to give to the world.
Mykl: Normal? Mykl? Bullshit. He reads weird magazines, seeks out bizarre experiences when he travels and let's face it, everyone is scared to ask him what he does for a crust. He can't help it if his IQ is so high everyone thinks he has Asperger’s. Mykl is like one of those strange nerds who, in Hollywood movies, comes up with the brilliant chemical formula which will save civilisation from some kind of huge plague. Sure, his personal life is a mess and we don't know when he last got laid, but do you want to save the world or not? Call him....
Myron: Myron stands for hours in front of a mirror, practising his various facial expressions in preparation for the next audition.
